review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting native-speaker review. House style: moderate Bokmål with three genders (ei/-a for feminine nouns, en/-en masculine, et/-et neuter), weak past in -et, neuter definite plural in -ene, sju and tjue, "ble", "ga". "ei seng / senga" is feminine; the house style writes the -a forms (sengen is also correct Bokmål).

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: Sam bor i et hus. Huset er stort.
sentences.english: Sam lives in a house. The house is big.

sentences.text: Sam har et rom i huset. Rommet er lite.
sentences.english: Sam has a room in the house. The room is small.

sentences.text: Det er ei seng i rommet. Senga er stor.
sentences.english: There is a bed in the room. The bed is big.

sentences.text: Rommet har også et vindu.
sentences.english: The room also has a window.

sentences.text: Vinduet er her. Sam liker vinduet.
sentences.english: The window is here. Sam likes the window.

sentences.text: Anna bor her. Hun jobber på klinikken.
sentences.english: Anna lives here. She works at the clinic.

sentences.text: Lars bor her også. Han er lærer på skolen.
sentences.english: Lars lives here too. He is a teacher at the school.

sentences.text: Marta bor ikke her. Hun bor i byen.
sentences.english: Marta does not live here. She lives in town.

sentences.text: Marta er bestemora til Nils. Nils bor ikke hos Marta.
sentences.english: Marta is Nils's grandmother. Nils does not live with Marta.

sentences.text: Nils bor hjemme. Han går på skolen.
sentences.english: Nils lives at home. He goes to school.

sentences.text: Hei, Sam! Hvordan går det?
sentences.english: Hi, Sam! How are you?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Det går bra, takk. Jeg er glad.
sentences.english: I am fine, thank you. I am happy.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Liker du huset?
sentences.english: Do you like the house?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Ja, jeg liker huset. Men jeg er trøtt i dag.
sentences.english: Yes, I like the house. But I am tired today.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Har du ei seng?
sentences.english: Do you have a bed?
sentences.speaker: ana

sentences.text: Ja, jeg har ei seng.
sentences.english: Yes, I have a bed.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Ja, det er bra. Rommet er lite, men jeg er glad.
sentences.english: Yes, that is good. The room is small, but I am happy.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Lars er hjemme. Han er trøtt.
sentences.english: Lars is at home. He is tired.

sentences.text: Hei, Sam! Kommer du til kirka i dag?
sentences.english: Hi, Sam! Are you coming to church today?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Ja, gjerne!
sentences.english: Yes, gladly!
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Bra! Vil du ha kaffe?
sentences.english: Good! Do you want coffee?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Ja, takk!
sentences.english: Yes, please!
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Fru Berg bor ikke i huset. Hun kommer fra byen, og hun er glad i Sam.
sentences.english: Mrs Berg does not live in the house. She comes from town, and she is fond of Sam.
